subject: radiology
title: Ablation and liver-directed cancer therapy

steps.tx: Heat, cold and electricity all kill focal tumours. **Radiofrequency ablation** heats tissue to coagulative necrosis and suits small **hepatocellular carcinomas** within transplant criteria. **Microwave ablation** reaches higher temperatures faster with less **heat-sink** loss near vessels. **Cryoablation** freezes with visible ice balls and suits renal tumours near the collecting system. **Irreversible electroporation** uses electric pulses without heat, suiting tumours hugging bile ducts or vessels.
steps.say: Heat, cold and electricity kill focal tumours. Radiofrequency heats small liver cancers to necrosis. Microwave runs hotter with less heat loss near vessels. Freezing suits kidney tumours near drainage tubes, and electroporation suits tumours hugging ducts without heat.

steps.tx: Selection decides ablation success. **Hepatocellular carcinoma** within **Milan criteria** under AASLD and EASL guidance suits ablation or transplant pathways. **Colorectal liver metastases** limited in number and size suit ablation when surgery is refused or unfit. **Heat-sink** from adjacent vessels over 3 mm cools radiofrequency zones and invites recurrence at the vessel edge. **Subcapsular tumours** risk seeding and bleeding, needing tract ablation on withdrawal. **Biopsy first** confirms histology before destroying the evidence.
steps.say: Selection decides success. Liver cancers within Milan criteria suit ablation or transplant routes. Limited colorectal secondaries suit ablation when surgery is refused. Vessel cooling causes edge recurrence, subcapsular tumours need tract burning, and biopsy must precede destruction.

steps.tx: Chemoembolisation pairs ischaemia with drugs. **Conventional TACE** mixes chemotherapy with lipiodol followed by embolic particles for intermediate **hepatocellular carcinoma**. **Drug-eluting bead TACE** releases drug slowly with less systemic toxicity. **Post-embolisation syndrome** with fever and pain follows and needs supportive care. **Liver failure** threatens when portal flow is already compromised, so **portal vein patency** is confirmed first. **Bilirubin and performance status** gate every session.
steps.say: Chemoembolisation pairs ischaemia with drugs. Conventional TACE mixes drugs with oil then particles for intermediate liver cancer. Bead TACE releases drug slowly with less toxicity. Fever and pain after need supportive care, and portal patency with bilirubin gates every session.

steps.tx: Radioembolisation irradiates from inside. **Yttrium-90 microspheres** lodge in tumour arterioles delivering **beta radiation** over days, suiting unresectable liver tumours with good reserve. A **macroaggregated albumin scan** maps **lung shunting** and gastrointestinal reflux before dosing, and excessive shunt cancels or reduces treatment. **Radiation segmentectomy** ablates small segments with high dose, while lobar treatment needs preserved function. **Gastric ulceration** from refluxed spheres is the dreaded non-target injury.
steps.say: Radioembolisation irradiates from inside. Yttrium spheres lodge in tumour vessels delivering beta dose over days. An albumin scan maps lung shunt and gut reflux first, with excess shunt cancelling treatment. Segmentectomy ablates small areas, and refluxed spheres ulcerate stomach.
